description.main: Daisuke Yokota's first book of colour work, published by Harper's Books and Flying Books in 2015 for his first US solo exhibition. 83 camera-less abstractions made by layering, heating and scanning unused large-format colour film, in a hardcover edition of 750 with five foil-colour cover variants.
description.extended:
Color Photographs is Daisuke Yokota's first book of colour work, published by Harper's Books and Flying Books in 2015 for his first solo exhibition in the United States, held at Harper's in East Hampton from 26 September to 1 December that year.

The 83 plates were made without a camera. Yokota layered sheets of unused large-format colour film, developed them by unorthodox means, including heat and boiling water that eroded and crystallised the emulsion, and scanned the results. The images are abstract, liquid and translucent, and read variously as fractal patterns or deep-space photographs. The hardcover edition of 750 copies is bound in silver cloth with the title foil-stamped on the front board. Five groups of 150 copies each carry a different foil colour: black, red, blue, green or yellow.

Yokota, born in Saitama in 1983, came to notice with the heavily reworked black-and-white images of Back Yard and Site/Cloud. In 2014 his Vertigo was shortlisted for the Paris Photo-Aperture PhotoBook Awards, and in 2015 he received the John Kobal Residency Award at Photo London. The colour experiments collected here extend his claim that the substance of photography lies in film and process rather than in the camera.
description.artist_bio: Daisuke Yokota (b. 1983, Saitama) lives and works in Tokyo. Represented by G/P Gallery, Tokyo. Awards include the Excellence Award at Canon New Cosmos of Photography 2008, the Grand Prize at 1_WALL 2010 and the John Kobal Residency Award at Photo London 2015. Vertigo (Newfave, 2014) was shortlisted for the Paris Photo-Aperture PhotoBook Awards.
description.exhibition_context: Published for Daisuke Yokota: Color Photographs, Harper's, East Hampton, 26 September to 1 December 2015, the artist's first solo exhibition in the United States.
